articles.title: Optimum Communications, Fluence Energy, Virgin Galactic And Other Big Stocks Moving Higher Today
articles.teaser: Several stocks, including Optimum Communications Services, surged while Dow fell. Technology, energy, and aerospace stocks saw notable gains.
articles.body:
U.S. stocks traded lower during today's session, with the Dow falling more than 65 points on Monday. However, several technology, energy, and aerospace stocks posted notable gains.

Shares of Optimum Communications Services Inc. (NYSE:OPTU) rose sharply to lead the list of top percentage gainers.  The company announced a tender offer to buy back up to 120 million of its shares at $2.50 per share.

The buyback represents about 42.5% of the issued and outstanding shares of Class A Common Stock as of May 27, 2026. The tender offer will expire at 5:00 pm (ET) on June 30, 2026.

Optimum Communications Services surged 93.71% to $1.27 on Monday.

Here are some other big stocks recording gains in today’s session.

  • Fluence Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ:FLNC) jumped 34.58% to $25.41.
  • Virgin Galactic Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:SPCE) gained 28.80% to $7.96, continuing the strong upward momentum from late last week. Stock market traders are rapidly accumulating positions in the space tourism pioneer, driven by several high-profile catalysts.
  • The Elmet Group Holdings Limited (NASDAQ:ELMT) climbed 25.0% to $19.10. The company reported strong first quarter earnings, with revenue up 20.7% to $56 million.
  • Taylor Morrison Home Corporation (NYSE:TMHC) advanced 22.46% to $71.64, following the announcement that Berkshire Hathaway has agreed to acquire the company in a $6.8 billion deal.
  • Edgewise Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:EWTX) rose 14.72% to $39.19, after the company announced the sale of its muscular dystrophy business to Servier for $2.65 billion.
  • Arm Holdings plc (NASDAQ:ARM) gained 13.63% to $401.47, after Nvidia unveiled its new RTX Spark chip, based on Arm Holdings' designs.
  • Replimune Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:REPL) climbed 13.0% to $9.82. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) prioritized the resubmission of the company's experimental advanced melanoma drug, RP1.
  • AirJoule Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ:AIRJ) advanced 12.9% to $5.07.
  • Asana, Inc. (NYSE:ASAN) rose 12.85% to $8.69.

articles.title: Taylor Morrison Home Surges On Berkshire Hathaway Acquisition, Joins Elmet Group And Other Big Stocks Moving Higher In Monday's Session
articles.teaser: U.S. stock futures up, Nasdaq surges 0.35%, with Taylor Morrison's buyout announcement. Other pre-market gainers include ELMT, PURR, and SPCE.
articles.body:
U.S. stock futures were higher this morning, with the Nasdaq futures surging more than 0.35% on Monday following a strong start to the month and massive acquisition headlines across the consumer and infrastructure sectors.

Shares of Taylor Morrison Home Corp (NYSE:TMHC) skyrocketed in pre-market trading following a definitive buyout announcement from Warren Buffett’s conglomerate.

Berkshire Hathaway agreed to purchase the homebuilder for approximately $8.5 billion in an all-cash transaction. This represents a 24% premium over Taylor Morrison's previous closing price of $58.50. The transaction, which is subject to standard regulatory clearances and shareholder approvals, is expected to close in the latter half of 2026.

Taylor Morrison shares jumped 22.85% to $71.87 in pre-market trading.

Here are some other stocks moving higher in pre-market trading:

  • The Elmet Group Co (NASDAQ:ELMT) shares surged 30.28% to $19.91 in pre-market trading on high speculative volume following trailing structural reorganizations and defense supply contract expansions.
  • Hyperliquid Strategies Inc (NASDAQ:PURR) climbed 20.82% to $12.07 in pre-market trading, catching strong momentum from weekend decentralized trading protocol volume spikes and ecosystem expansion updates.
  • Virgin Galactic Holdings Inc (NYSE:SPCE) rose 18.71% to $7.34 in pre-market trading.
  • ARM Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:ARM) pushed 12.85% higher to $398.70 in pre-market trading after gaining 4.19% on Friday.
  • IBM Common Stock (NYSE:IBM) rose 12.62% to $335.40 in pre-market trading, building on sustained buying pressure as the company continues to gain institutional inflows following its headline plans to deploy $10 billion toward commercial quantum systems by 2029.
  • Jade Biosciences Inc (NASDAQ:JBIO) advanced 11.83% to $23.53 in pre-market trading.
  • Alpha Metallurgical Resources Inc (NYSE:AMR) gained 11.77% to $222.39 in pre-market trading after declining by 6.90% on Friday.
  • ServiceNow Inc (NYSE:NOW) surged 11.24% to $138.35 in pre-market trading, finding momentum after updating its enterprise generative AI automation software workflows for global cloud clients.
  • KRAKacquisition Corp (NASDAQ:KRAQ) ticked up 10.58% to $10.97 in pre-market trading.

articles.title: 'Hated' Homebuilder Stocks Making A Comeback? Jim Cramer Thinks Berkshire Hathaway's $6.8 Billion Taylor Morrison Deal Maybe Small But It Has Value
articles.teaser: Jim Cramer said Berkshire's $6.8 billion Taylor Morrison deal signals value in homebuilder stocks shunned by Wall Street.
articles.body:
Jim Cramer said Sunday Berkshire Hathaway Inc’s (NYSE:BRK) (NYSE:BRK) planned acquisition of Taylor Morrison Home Corp. (NYSE:TMHC) for $6.8 billion may offer investors a reason to take another look at homebuilder stocks, arguing that the deal suggests value could be emerging in a sector that has largely fallen out of favor on Wall Street.

“Berkshire Hathaway buying Taylor Morrison, small deal, but shows that there may be value in the hated homebuilders,” Cramer wrote in a post on X following news of the acquisition.

What Berkshire May Be Seeing

Berkshire’s move suggests it sees value where much of Wall Street remains cautious.

Homebuilder stocks have faced pressure from elevated mortgage rates and affordability concerns, leaving the sector largely out of favor with investors.

The acquisition could signal confidence in the long-term housing market despite near-term headwinds, where for investors, Berkshire’s willingness to commit billions to the sector may support Cramer view that value still exists in a group many investors have written off.

A signal for investors

Investors watch Berkshire’s deal making activity for clues about market opportunities, with even relatively small acquisitions sparking discussions about whether a sector has become undervalued.

The purchase of Taylor Morrison may also draw attention to other publicly traded homebuilders, including D.R. Horton (NYSE:DHI), Lennar (NYSE:LEN) and PulteGroup (NYSE:PHM), as investors assess whether Berkshire’s move reflects a broader opportunity in the group.

"Berkshire is acquiring a best-in-class national homebuilder, led by an exceptional team and backed by a trusted reputation for customer experience," said Berkshire CEO Greg Abel said in a statement.

The acquisition marks the first major deal for Warren Buffet’s successor Abel, who took over as CEO in January.

Read Also: Hewlett Packard, Science Applications And 3 Stocks To Watch Heading Into Monday

Not Berkshire’s First Housing Bet

The conglomerate already has exposure to the sector through businesses including their 2003 acquisition Clayton Homes, one of the largest manufactured-home builders in the United States.

“It would be something if Berkshire put up prefab homes from Clayton on all of that land that Taylor Morrison has,” Cramer added.

At Friday’s close, shares of Berkshire Hathaway’s Class A and Class B shares fell 0.6%, while Taylor Morrison closed 0.4% lower.

Benzinga Edge Rankings indicate that Berkshire Hathaway’s Class A and Class B shares has a Momentum score in the 18th percentile and a Growth score in the 89th percentile.

Benzinga Edge Rankings indicate that Taylor Morrison shares have a Momentum score in the 19th percentile and a Growth score in the 75th percentile.
